proofs.proof_tex:
Define the target-arm causal identified sets
\[
 \Theta_{a,\mathrm{tar}}^r(P)
 =\{\theta_a(Q):Q\in\mathcal Q^r(P)\},\qquad
 \Theta_{\Delta,\mathrm{tar}}^r(P)
 =\{\Delta_{d,e}(Q):Q\in\mathcal Q^r(P)\},                       \tag{38}
\]
and define \(\Theta_{a,\mathrm{BK}}^r(P)\) and \(\Theta_{\Delta,\mathrm{BK}}^r(P)\) by replacing \(\mathcal Q^r(P)\) in (38) with \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{BK}}^r(P)\).  These are causal sets; the observed-law functionals \(\mathcal I_a^r(P)\) and \(\mathcal I_\Delta^r(P)\) will be shown to equal their closures, not defined to do so.

We first establish sharpness for the target-arm class.  Fix eligible signs \(b\in\mathcal B_d^r(P)\) and \(h\in\mathcal B_e^r(P)\), and choose exactly support-admissible marginal completions for the two arms.  Let \(K_{a,j}\) denote the chosen conditional law of \(Y_a\) in cell \(j\).  On a factual cell \(j\in\mathcal O_a\), compatibility and consistency require \(Y_a=Y\); on a missing cell, \(K_{a,j}\) has support \([\ell_a,u_a]\) and the chosen feasible mean.

Draw \((Y,D,Z)\sim P\).  Conditional on \((Y,D,Z)\), set \(Y_a=Y\) whenever \(D=a\), and for every missing target arm draw \(Y_a\) from \(K_{a,j}\), independently across arms given the observed data.  Each target potential outcome then has exactly its selected cellwise marginal law.  Consequently, the construction preserves \(Q_{Y,D,Z}=P\), consistency, each aggregate support, and each armwise score moment.  Conditional independence is only a coupling device and is not imposed on the model.

It follows that every pair of exactly attainable means from the selected branches is jointly attainable in \(\mathcal Q^r(P)\).  By \(\text{thm:support-eligibility}\), those attainable means are dense in
\[
 [L_{d,b}^r(P),U_{d,b}^r(P)]
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 [L_{e,h}^r(P),U_{e,h}^r(P)].
\]
Their differences are therefore dense in
\[
 [L_{d,b}^r(P)-U_{e,h}^r(P),
   U_{d,b}^r(P)-L_{e,h}^r(P)].                                  \tag{39}
\]
Conversely, \(\text{lem:branch-reduction}\) places the two means induced by every \(Q\in\mathcal Q^r(P)\) in closures of eligible branch images.  The finite union over \((b,h)\), together with \(\text{def:arm-closure}\) and \(\text{def:ate-closure}\), therefore gives
\[
 \operatorname{cl}\Theta_{a,\mathrm{tar}}^r(P)=\mathcal I_a^r(P),
 \qquad
 \operatorname{cl}\Theta_{\Delta,\mathrm{tar}}^r(P)=\mathcal I_\Delta^r(P). \tag{19a}
\]

We now compare the target-arm and all-arm classes.  The definition gives \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{BK}}^r(P)\subseteq\mathcal Q^r(P)\), so both Ban--K\'edagni identified sets are contained in their target-arm counterparts.  For the reverse inclusion, use the assumed nonemptiness to fix \(Q^0\in\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{BK}}^r(P)\), and fix an arbitrary \(Q^1\in\mathcal Q^r(P)\).  In each observed cell, retain from \(Q^1\) the conditional marginal kernels of \(Y_d\) and \(Y_e\), and retain from \(Q^0\) the conditional marginal kernel of every \(Y_a\) with \(a\notin\{d,e\}\).  Draw \((Y,D,Z)\sim P\); set \(Y_D=Y\); and, conditional on the observed data, product-couple all remaining potential outcomes from the retained kernels.

For each target arm, the resulting law has the same cellwise marginal kernels as \(Q^1\), so it preserves that law's target means, score restrictions, and aggregate supports.  For every untargeted arm, it has the same cellwise marginal kernels as \(Q^0\), so it preserves the corresponding all-arm restrictions.  Compatibility and consistency hold by construction.  Because the maintained class contains no restriction involving two distinct potential-outcome arms, no defining condition is changed by replacing the original cross-arm dependence with this conditional product coupling.  The resulting law \(\widetilde Q\) therefore belongs to \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{BK}}^r(P)\) and satisfies
\[
 \theta_d(\widetilde Q)=\theta_d(Q^1),\qquad
 \theta_e(\widetilde Q)=\theta_e(Q^1),\qquad
 \Delta_{d,e}(\widetilde Q)=\Delta_{d,e}(Q^1).                    \tag{19b}
\]
Since \(Q^1\) was arbitrary, (19b) proves the reverse inclusions and hence equality of the exact identified sets.  Combining that equality with (19a) proves the asserted sharp closures.  If \(\mathcal A=\{d,e\}\), there are no untargeted arms, so the two class definitions coincide.  The nonempty all-arm premise is essential to the extension argument: without \(Q^0\), admissible untargeted-arm kernels need not exist.

added_lemmas.statement:
Along \((P_\varepsilon)\) under SDC, for \(0<\varepsilon<3/110\),
\[
 \tau_{1,+}^{\mathrm{SDC}}(P_\varepsilon)=\frac{3\varepsilon}{2},\qquad
 \tau_{1,-}^{\mathrm{SDC}}(P_\varepsilon)=\frac25-\frac{\varepsilon}{2},
\]
and both arm-zero branches have total slack one, attained at the missing-mean vector \((1/2,1/2)\).  Thus the minimum positive branch slack is \(3\varepsilon/2\).  The arm-one closure is \([3/5,4/5]\) at \(\varepsilon=0\) and
\[
 [3/10+\varepsilon/4,3/10+\varepsilon]
 \mathbin{\cup}[3/5+\varepsilon/2,4/5+\varepsilon/4]
\]
for positive \(\varepsilon\), whereas the arm-zero closure is always \([1/4,3/4]\).  Consequently, the ATE closures are \([-3/20,11/20]\) at zero and \([-9/20+\varepsilon/4,11/20+\varepsilon/4]\) for positive \(\varepsilon\), and both set maps are Hausdorff-discontinuous at zero.  Moreover,
\[
 \chi^2(P_\varepsilon\Vert P_0)=\frac{\varepsilon^2}{4v_0}
 =\frac{275}{21}\varepsilon^2,
 \qquad v_0=\frac{21}{1100},
\]
and
\[
 \chi^2(P_\varepsilon^n\Vert P_0^n)
 =\left(1+\frac{\varepsilon^2}{4v_0}\right)^n-1.
\]
For every \(q\in\{\mathrm{arm},\mathrm{ATE}\}\) and every deterministic positive sequence \(\varepsilon_n=o(n^{-1/2})\), the known-pair two-point decision problem satisfies
\[
 \lim_{n\to\infty}\inf_{\widehat I_n}
 \max_{P\in\{P_0,P_{\varepsilon_n}\}}
 \mathbb E_{P^n}\!\left[
 \rho_H\!\left(\widehat I_n,\mathcal I_{\partial,q}(P)\right)\right]
 =\frac{3}{20},
\]
where the infimum is over measurable estimators taking values in the nonempty compact subsets of \(\mathbb R\) and allowed to depend on the displayed two-point experiment.  The result is SDC-only and makes no LEI boundary assertion.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Let \(f_0\) be the \(\operatorname{Beta}(3,7)\) density and write expectation under \(f_0\) as \(\mathbb E_0\).  Direct beta-integral ratios give
\[
 \mu_0:=\mathbb E_0Y=\frac3{10},\qquad
 v_0:=\mathbb E_0[(Y-\mu_0)^2]
 =\frac{3\cdot7}{(3+7)^2(3+7+1)}=\frac{21}{1100}.                 \tag{22}
\]
The tilted density in \(\text{def:boundary-family}\) is
\[
 f_\varepsilon(y)=f_0(y)\left\{1+\varepsilon\frac{y-\mu_0}{v_0}\right\}.
\]
Its bracket integrates to one because \(\mathbb E_0(Y-\mu_0)=0\).  If \(0\le\varepsilon<3/110\), its minimum on \([0,1]\) is \(1-\varepsilon(3/10)/v_0>0\); if \(-3/110<\varepsilon<0\), its minimum is \(1-|\varepsilon|(7/10)/v_0>0\).  Thus every tilted factual law has topological support \([0,1]\).  Moreover,
\[
 \mathbb E_\varepsilon Y
 =\mu_0+\frac{\varepsilon}{v_0}\mathbb E_0[Y(Y-\mu_0)]
 =\mu_0+\varepsilon,                                             \tag{23}
\]
because \(\mathbb E_0[Y(Y-\mu_0)]=v_0\).  The other treated factual mean, from \(\operatorname{Beta}(9,1)\), is \(9/10\).

The cell masses in \(\text{def:boundary-family}\) give \(\mu_D=\mu_Z=1/2\).  Let \(x\in[0,1]\) be the missing mean of \(Y_1\) in cell \((D,Z)=(0,0)\).  Consistency fixes the other two cell means at \(9/10\) and \(3/10+\varepsilon\).  Finite summation therefore gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \theta_1&=\frac{3}{10}+\frac{\varepsilon}{4}+\frac{x}{2},\\
 \operatorname{Cov}(Y_1,D)&=\frac{3}{20}+\frac{\varepsilon}{8}-\frac{x}{4},\\
 \operatorname{Cov}(Y_1,Z)&=\frac{3\varepsilon}{8}-\frac{x}{4}.
 \end{aligned}                                                    \tag{24}
\]
For \(0<\varepsilon<3/110\), both covariances in (24) are nonnegative exactly when
\[
 0\le x\le\frac{3\varepsilon}{2}.
\]
The first covariance is then strictly positive, since \(x\le3\varepsilon/2<3/5+\varepsilon/2\).  This is the positive SDC branch.  It has one slack coordinate, so \(\text{def:interior-slack}\) and \(3\varepsilon/2<1/2\) give
\[
 \tau_{1,+}^{\mathrm{SDC}}(P_\varepsilon)
 =\max_{0\le x\le3\varepsilon/2}\min\{x,1-x\}
 =\frac{3\varepsilon}{2}.                                      \tag{25}
\]
Its linear mean image is \([3/10+\varepsilon/4,3/10+\varepsilon]\).  Both covariances are nonpositive exactly when
\[
 \frac35+\frac{\varepsilon}{2}\le x\le1,
\]
which is the negative branch.  Since its lower endpoint exceeds \(1/2\),
\[
 \tau_{1,-}^{\mathrm{SDC}}(P_\varepsilon)
 =\max_{3/5+\varepsilon/2\le x\le1}\min\{x,1-x\}
 =\frac25-\frac{\varepsilon}{2},                                \tag{26}
\]
and its mean image is \([3/5+\varepsilon/2,4/5+\varepsilon/4]\).  At \(\varepsilon=0\), the positive branch is the singleton box vertex \(x=0\), hence has zero slack and is excluded by \(\text{thm:support-eligibility}\); the negative branch gives \([3/5,4/5]\).

For arm zero, let \(u,v\in[0,1]\) be the missing means in cells \((1,0)\) and \((1,2)\).  The observed uniform cell has mean \(1/2\), and direct summation yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \theta_0&=\frac14+\frac{u}{4}+\frac{v}{4},\\
 \operatorname{Cov}(Y_0,D)&=-\frac18+\frac{u}{8}+\frac{v}{8},\\
 \operatorname{Cov}(Y_0,Z)&=-\frac18-\frac{u}{8}+\frac{3v}{8}.
 \end{aligned}                                                    \tag{27}
\]
The positive branch is the intersection of the unit square with \(u+v\ge1\) and \(3v-u\ge1\); its mean image is \([1/2,3/4]\), with endpoints attained at \((1/2,1/2)\) and \((1,1)\).  The negative branch reverses both inequalities and has mean image \([1/4,1/2]\), with endpoints attained at \((0,0)\) and \((1/2,1/2)\).  At \((u,v)=(1/2,1/2)\), both score coordinates vanish, so the point belongs to both branches.  For every feasible \((u,v)\), the total slack is at most
\[
 \min\{u,1-u\}+\min\{v,1-v\}\le1,
\]
and equality is attained at \((1/2,1/2)\) with slack vector \((1/2,1/2)\).  Hence
\[
 \tau_{0,+}^{\mathrm{SDC}}(P_\varepsilon)
 =\tau_{0,-}^{\mathrm{SDC}}(P_\varepsilon)=1,
 \qquad
 \mathcal I_0^{\mathrm{SDC}}(P_\varepsilon)=[1/4,3/4].           \tag{28}
\]
Because \(0<\varepsilon<3/110<1/5\), (25), (26), and (28) show that the minimum positive slack over all four branches is \(3\varepsilon/2\).

All factual conditional laws have support \([0,1]\).  On each eligible branch choose an interior feasible missing mean and a full-support distribution on \([0,1]\) with that mean.  Such a distribution exists, for example a beta law with positive parameters.  Setting each factual potential outcome equal to \(Y\) and conditionally product-coupling the missing kernels produces a compatible binary-treatment full-data law.  Thus the all-arm class is nonempty here, and \(\text{prop:ate-product-coupling}\), together with \(\text{thm:support-eligibility}\), permits simultaneous choice of the two target-arm completions.  Subtracting (28) from the arm-one interval at zero gives
\[
 \mathcal I_\Delta^{\mathrm{SDC}}(P_0)=[-3/20,11/20].             \tag{29}
\]
For positive \(\varepsilon\), the two component differences are
\[
 [-9/20+\varepsilon/4,\ 1/20+\varepsilon]
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 [-3/20+\varepsilon/2,\ 11/20+\varepsilon/4].                    \tag{30}
\]
They overlap because \(-3/20+\varepsilon/2\le1/20+\varepsilon\), so their union is \([-9/20+\varepsilon/4,11/20+\varepsilon/4]\).

Put \(I_{q,0}=\mathcal I_{\partial,q}(P_0)\) and \(I_{q,\varepsilon}=\mathcal I_{\partial,q}(P_\varepsilon)\).  For the arm map, the left endpoint \(3/10+\varepsilon/4\) of the new low component is at distance \(3/10-\varepsilon/4\) from \([3/5,4/5]\), while every point in the shifted high component and every point of the old interval is within \(\varepsilon/2\) of the other set.  Since \(\varepsilon<3/110\), the former distance is larger.  For the ATE map, (29)--(30) are intervals whose lower endpoints differ by \(3/10-\varepsilon/4\) and whose upper endpoints differ by \(\varepsilon/4\).  Hence, for both \(q\),
\[
 d_H(I_{q,0},I_{q,\varepsilon})
 =\frac3{10}-\frac{\varepsilon}{4}.                             \tag{31}
\]
The right side tends to \(3/10\), proving Hausdorff discontinuity.

It remains to establish the exact statistical frontier.  Let \(L_\varepsilon=dP_\varepsilon/dP_0\).  Only the cell \((D,Z)=(1,2)\), of \(P_0\)-probability \(1/4\), changes.  On that cell,
\[
 L_\varepsilon=1+\varepsilon\frac{Y-\mu_0}{v_0},
\]
and it equals one elsewhere.  Therefore, using (22),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \chi^2(P_\varepsilon\Vert P_0)
 &=\mathbb E_{P_0}(L_\varepsilon-1)^2\\
 &=\frac14\frac{\varepsilon^2}{v_0^2}
   \mathbb E_0[(Y-\mu_0)^2]
 =\frac{\varepsilon^2}{4v_0}
 =\frac{275}{21}\varepsilon^2.                                  \tag{32}
 \end{aligned}
\]
Independence under \(\text{ass:iid}\) gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 1+\chi^2(P_\varepsilon^n\Vert P_0^n)
 &=\mathbb E_{P_0^n}\left[\prod_{i=1}^nL_\varepsilon(O_i)^2\right]\\
 &=\{\mathbb E_{P_0}L_\varepsilon(O)^2\}^n
 =\left(1+\frac{\varepsilon^2}{4v_0}\right)^n.                   \tag{33}
 \end{aligned}
\]
For any \(Q\ll P\), Cauchy--Schwarz applied to \(dQ/dP-1\) yields
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q,P)
 =\frac12\mathbb E_P\left|\frac{dQ}{dP}-1\right|
 \le\frac12\sqrt{\chi^2(Q\Vert P)}.                             \tag{34}
\]
If \(\varepsilon_n=o(n^{-1/2})\), then \(n\varepsilon_n^2\to0\), and (33), the inequality \((1+t)^n\le e^{nt}\), and (34) imply
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(P_{\varepsilon_n}^n,P_0^n)\longrightarrow0.   \tag{34a}
\]

We finally prove both sides of the exact minimax limit.  For fixed \(q\), let \(A_n=I_{q,0}\), \(B_n=I_{q,\varepsilon_n}\), and \(\delta_n=d_H(A_n,B_n)\).  Eventually \(\delta_n<1\), so \(\rho_H(A_n,B_n)=\delta_n\).  If two laws \(Q_0,Q_1\) have densities \(q_0,q_1\) relative to a common dominating measure and \(I_0,I_1\) are their two nonempty compact targets, the measure with density \(q_0\wedge q_1\) has mass \(1-\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)\).  The triangle inequality for the metric \(\rho_H\) then gives, for every estimator \(\widehat I_n\),
\[
 \max_{i=0,1}\mathbb E_{Q_i}\rho_H(\widehat I_n,I_i)
 \ge\frac{\rho_H(I_0,I_1)}{2}
       \{1-\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)\}.                         \tag{34b}
\]
Indeed, integrate \(\rho_H(\widehat I_n,I_0)+\rho_H(\widehat I_n,I_1)\ge\rho_H(I_0,I_1)\) against that common submeasure, and bound the two integrals by their respective risks.  Taking \((Q_0,Q_1)=(P_0^n,P_{\varepsilon_n}^n)\), (31), (34a), and (34b) yield the lower limit \(3/20\).

For the matching upper bound, we construct a deterministic Hausdorff midpoint.  For nonempty compact \(A,B\subset\mathbb R\), set \(\delta=d_H(A,B)\) and
\[
 M(A,B)=\left\{\frac{a+b}{2}:a\in A,\ b\in B,\ |a-b|\le\delta\right\}.
\]
The set is nonempty and compact.  Every point of \(M(A,B)\) is within \(\delta/2\) of both \(A\) and \(B\).  Conversely, the definition of Hausdorff distance and compactness give, for every \(a\in A\), a \(b\in B\) with \(|a-b|\le\delta\), and conversely for every \(b\in B\); the corresponding midpoint is within \(\delta/2\).  Hence
\[
 d_H(A,M(A,B))=d_H(B,M(A,B))=\frac\delta2.                       \tag{34c}
\]
where equality follows from the triangle inequality after the two upper bounds.  In the known two-point experiment, the constant estimator \(M(A_n,B_n)\) is measurable and has maximal risk \(\delta_n/2\).  Thus the minimax risk is at most \(\delta_n/2\), which tends to \(3/20\) by (31).  Together with the lower bound this proves the asserted limit.  Finally, (25) shows that the minimum positive slack along the alternative is \(\kappa_n=3\varepsilon_n/2=o(n^{-1/2})\), yet the minimax risk does not shrink.  Every calculation used SDC alone; no LEI conclusion follows.
added_lemmas.justification: The theorem identifies the exact statistical cost of a disappearing support-eligible branch through a root-\(n\) indistinguishable SDC experiment.
added_lemmas.gap: Generic LP nonregularity does not provide this legal SDC family, its exact branch slacks and set jump, or the exact \(3/20\) known-pair minimax limit.
added_lemmas.consumer: Inference procedures can be screened against a certified nonshrinking frontier even when the smallest positive branch slack is \(o(n^{-1/2})\).

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Let \(\mathcal Q^r(P)\), equivalently \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{tar}}^r(P)\), denote the class imposing aggregate support and the correlation restriction only on \(\{d,e\}\), and let \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{BK}}^r(P)\) impose those armwise restrictions for every \(a\in\mathcal A\).  The class definitions contain no restriction coupling distinct potential-outcome arms.  If \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{BK}}^r(P)\ne\varnothing\), then, for \(a\in\{d,e\}\),
\[
 \{\theta_a(Q):Q\in\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{BK}}^r(P)\}
 =\{\theta_a(Q):Q\in\mathcal Q^r(P)\},
\]
and
\[
 \{\Delta_{d,e}(Q):Q\in\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{BK}}^r(P)\}
 =\{\Delta_{d,e}(Q):Q\in\mathcal Q^r(P)\}.
\]
Their arm-mean closures are \(\mathcal I_a^r(P)\), and their ATE closure is \(\mathcal I_\Delta^r(P)\).  In particular, conditional product coupling establishes joint endpoint approximation rather than merely subtracting marginal outer bounds.  When \(\mathcal A=\{d,e\}\), the two classes are identical.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The frozen notation describes a target-arm class, not Ban--Kédagni's all-arm class when treatment is multivalued. The replacement restricts the published-class equality to laws for which the all-arm class is nonempty, distinguishes the two classes, and proves equality of their exact target-arm and ATE identified sets before taking closures.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Theorem 3 certifies the following nonshrinking frontier for the binary-treatment fixed-grid SDC model: if \(\varepsilon_n>0\), \(\varepsilon_n=o(n^{-1/2})\), and \(\kappa_n=3\varepsilon_n/2\), then the smallest positive branch slack at \(P_{\varepsilon_n}\) is \(\kappa_n\), while the known-pair minimax Hausdorff risk over \(\{P_0,P_{\varepsilon_n}\}\) converges to \(3/20\) for both the arm and ATE closures.  Beyond this proved frontier, can \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{adapt}}\) be completed into a computable region \(\widetilde{\mathcal C}_n\) that is uniformly honest for \(\mathcal I_\Delta^r(P)\) over the binary-treatment fixed-grid model, contracts at a specified regular LP-value rate on classes separated from every branch-eligibility boundary by explicit slack, cell-mass, and, in LEI mode, variance margins, and attains a matching lower frontier?  The requested construction must state its loss or size criterion, critical value, and conditioning margins; no contraction exponent is asserted from slack alone.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The explicit family now settles the nonshrinking frontier for \(\kappa_n=o(n^{-1/2})\). The remaining question is narrowed to construction and optimal rates under fully specified loss, slack, cell-mass, and LEI-variance margins; it no longer presents the proved frontier as open.

proposed.statement:
Let \(\mathcal Q^r(P)\), equivalently \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{tar}}^r(P)\), denote the class imposing aggregate support and the correlation restriction only on \(\{d,e\}\), and let \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{BK}}^r(P)\) impose those armwise restrictions for every \(a\in\mathcal A\).  The class definitions contain no restriction coupling distinct potential-outcome arms.  If \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{BK}}^r(P)\ne\varnothing\), then, for \(a\in\{d,e\}\),
\[
 \{\theta_a(Q):Q\in\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{BK}}^r(P)\}
 =\{\theta_a(Q):Q\in\mathcal Q^r(P)\},
\]
and
\[
 \{\Delta_{d,e}(Q):Q\in\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{BK}}^r(P)\}
 =\{\Delta_{d,e}(Q):Q\in\mathcal Q^r(P)\}.
\]
Their arm-mean closures are \(\mathcal I_a^r(P)\), and their ATE closure is \(\mathcal I_\Delta^r(P)\).  In particular, conditional product coupling establishes joint endpoint approximation rather than merely subtracting marginal outer bounds.  When \(\mathcal A=\{d,e\}\), the two classes are identical.
proposed.justification: The coupling establishes joint target-arm attainment and also shows when the target-arm calculation is faithful to Ban--Kédagni's all-arm published class.
proposed.gap: Park2025 treats joint attainment under MIV plus MTR; it does not supply this conditional-product witness for armwise SDC, exact aggregate support, or extension from target-arm to all-arm restrictions.
proposed.consumer: Finite-valued-treatment users may report the exact ATE closure for the published all-arm class when that class is nonempty, while binary-treatment applications obtain the result without a class distinction.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Add the all-arm class dependency and the symbols used by the corrected published-class comparison.

proposed.statement: Theorem 3 certifies the following nonshrinking frontier for the binary-treatment fixed-grid SDC model: if \(\varepsilon_n>0\), \(\varepsilon_n=o(n^{-1/2})\), and \(\kappa_n=3\varepsilon_n/2\), then the smallest positive branch slack at \(P_{\varepsilon_n}\) is \(\kappa_n\), while the known-pair minimax Hausdorff risk over \(\{P_0,P_{\varepsilon_n}\}\) converges to \(3/20\) for both the arm and ATE closures.  Beyond this proved frontier, can \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{adapt}}\) be completed into a computable region \(\widetilde{\mathcal C}_n\) that is uniformly honest for \(\mathcal I_\Delta^r(P)\) over the binary-treatment fixed-grid model, contracts at a specified regular LP-value rate on classes separated from every branch-eligibility boundary by explicit slack, cell-mass, and, in LEI mode, variance margins, and attains a matching lower frontier?  The requested construction must state its loss or size criterion, critical value, and conditioning margins; no contraction exponent is asserted from slack alone.
proposed.justification: The remaining open content is an honest adaptation theorem beyond the now-certified \(o(n^{-1/2})\) nonshrinking slack frontier.
proposed.gap: Existing projection, perturbed-LP, and generic linear-system results do not derive a completion-slack-indexed optimal rate after simultaneously controlling loss, cell masses, and LEI variances.
proposed.consumer: A solution would replace conservative whole-set projection away from branch boundaries without contradicting the exact two-point impossibility theorem.

obligation.what_is_open: A computable uniformly honest adaptive region, a precise loss or size criterion, stable slack and conditioning margins, an achievable contraction rate, and a matching lower frontier beyond the proved root-\(n\) nonshrinking family.
obligation.obstruction: Slack alone does not control LP conditioning, small cell masses, or the standardized LEI scores, and the frozen handle does not specify a loss, studentization, or critical value. Inferring an exponent from slack alone would assume the crux.
obligation.attempted: Hoeffding projection supplies honesty, and the exact chi-square calculation plus the disappearing-branch family settles nonshrinking for \(\kappa_n=o(n^{-1/2})\). These ingredients do not yet calibrate an adaptive critical value or an optimal positive-margin modulus.
obligation.partial_result:
The closed results now give both a finite-sample honest fallback and an exact local impossibility frontier.  The projection region \(\mathcal C_n\) covers the entire sharp closure with probability at least \(1-\alpha\), including at zero slack.  Along the explicit SDC family,
\[
 \chi^2(P_{\varepsilon_n}^n\Vert P_0^n)
 =\left(1+\frac{275}{21}\varepsilon_n^2\right)^n-1\longrightarrow0
\]
whenever \(\varepsilon_n=o(n^{-1/2})\), while the smallest positive branch slack is
\[
 \kappa_n=\tau_{1,+}^{\mathrm{SDC}}(P_{\varepsilon_n})
 =\frac{3\varepsilon_n}{2}=o(n^{-1/2}).
\]
For both \(q=\mathrm{arm}\) and \(q=\mathrm{ATE}\),
\[
 \lim_{n\to\infty}\inf_{\widehat I_n}
 \max_{P\in\{P_0,P_{\varepsilon_n}\}}
 \mathbb E_{P^n}\rho_H\!\left(\widehat I_n,
 \mathcal I_{\partial,q}(P)\right)=\frac{3}{20}.
\]
Thus uniform shrinking fails even along positive-slack alternatives with \(\kappa_n=o(n^{-1/2})\).  What remains open is a computable adaptive procedure and a matching rate theorem after the loss and the necessary slack, cell-mass, and LEI-variance conditioning margins are all fixed.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Remove the now-settled root-\(n\) nonshrinking frontier from the open content and update its scoped obligation without resolving the remaining adaptive problem.

prose_updates.tldr: For finite imperfect-instrument cells, SDC and SDC-plus-LEI reduce target-arm identification to bounded completion polytopes, and exact aggregate support retains exactly the positive-slack branches. Unrestricted cone duals give sharp arm closures and conditional product coupling gives the sharp ATE closure; if the all-arm Ban--Kédagni class is nonempty, its exact target-arm and ATE identified sets coincide with those of the target-arm class. The rational center yields \([711/1100,911/1100]\), strictly inside the normalized outer union, and positive LP margins make this strict inclusion persist on an open two-parameter beta neighborhood of \((79/100,17/20)\). A legal three-cell SDC family has minimum positive slack \(3\varepsilon/2\), a fixed Hausdorff jump, and exact known-pair minimax risk \(3/20\) for every \(\varepsilon_n=o(n^{-1/2})\). Binary-treatment Hoeffding projection covers the whole exact set in finite samples.

project_justification.gap: Ban and Kédagni impose aggregate support equality for every treatment arm but report normalized valid outer bounds and leave sharpness unresolved. Their formulas neither filter algebraically feasible branches by exact support nor establish that target-arm calculations extend to the published all-arm class; an isolated numerical strictness witness would also leave robustness unclear.
project_justification.niche: Finite-cell correlation-cone geometry separates branch feasibility, positive-slack support eligibility, endpoint optimization, and cross-arm coupling. This separation yields an all-arm extension theorem under a nonempty published-class premise, an open neighborhood of strict improvement around an exact rational center, and an explicit SDC branch boundary whose statistical indistinguishability is governed by \(n\varepsilon^2\).
project_justification.fill: The paper supplies the positive-slack eligibility equivalence, unrestricted-cone sharp endpoints, exact target-arm and all-arm coupling logic, rational and locally robust strictness certificates, exact SDC discontinuity formulas, an exact \(3/20\) root-\(n\) two-point minimax frontier, and a conservative finite-sample whole-set confidence region.

sampling_model.treatment: The structural calculations allow finite-valued \(D_i\) and impose support and correlation restrictions on target arms \(d\) and \(e\) in \(\mathcal Q^r(P)\). The distinct class \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{BK}}^r(P)\) imposes them on every \(a\in\mathcal A\); the two classes coincide on the binary-treatment submodel used for inference.
sampling_model.overlap: The maintained target overlap is \(0<P(D=a)<1\) for \(a\in\{d,e\}\). Equality with the published all-arm identified sets additionally requires \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{BK}}^r(P)\ne\varnothing\), which supplies admissible untargeted-arm kernels rather than silently imposing extra target overlap.

prose_updates.related_work: Ban and Kédagni (2022) supply the all-arm aggregate-support and SDC or SDC-plus-LEI restrictions and valid normalized outer formulas. This paper's target-arm class equals their class on binary treatment; with multiple treatment levels, the exact target-arm and ATE identified sets agree under the explicit premise that the all-arm class is nonempty. The unrestricted cone result strictly tightens their normalized SDC union at the rational center \(P^\star\). With the four cell masses and uniform control cells fixed, the treated laws \(\operatorname{Beta}(100\varrho,100(1-\varrho))\) and \(\operatorname{Beta}(20s,20(1-s))\), centered at \((\varrho,s)=(79/100,17/20)\), retain strict inclusion on an open neighborhood by positive slack, score-feasibility, endpoint-gap, and multiplier margins. Kédagni, Li, and Mourifié (2018) study sharp finite zero-covariance restrictions, a different moment class. Nevo and Rosen (2012) motivate same-direction and less-endogenous correlations. Park (2025) proves joint attainment for a different MIV-plus-MTR problem and is not a tightening target. Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019), Cho and Russell (2024), Fang and Santos (2019), Bai et al. (2026), Goff and Mbakop (2026), Levis et al. (2025), and Chernozhukov, Lee, and Rosen (2013) inform generic projection, mathematical-program, nonsmooth, and intersection-bound inference; none supplies the exact support-filtered root-\(n\) frontier proved here. Ban--Kédagni's NLSYM application and Zhanhan Yu's PM2.5 application are same-population-restriction consumers: under the maintained restrictions, the reported population object changes from a valid normalized outer region to the exact support-filtered set with a branch-slack boundary diagnostic.
prose_updates.interpretation: The causal objects are the identified sets of \(\theta_a(Q)\) and \(\Delta_{d,e}(Q)\) over compatible full-data laws. The LP unions are observed-law functionals proved to equal the closures of those sets. Positive slack is an exact aggregate-support eligibility condition, not a numerical tolerance. Conditional product coupling proves that armwise endpoint approximations coexist on one full-data law and, when the published all-arm class is nonempty, that untargeted-arm restrictions do not change the target identified sets.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Exact decisions at \(\tau_{a,b}^r(P)=0\) require rational arithmetic, interval certificates, or explicit primal--dual tolerances. The local strictness neighborhood relies on finite-LP positive margins and does not assert global robustness. The exact \(3/20\) frontier concerns the known two-point SDC experiment and rules out shrinking along \(\kappa_n=o(n^{-1/2})\); it does not determine an adaptive rate from slack alone. The coverage construction is conservative and binary-treatment, and may require global optimization over positive-mass primitive pairs. Fixed grids, known support endpoints, and independent sampling are maintained; LEI boundary behavior, covariate adjustment, clustered sampling, estimated supports, empirical sign reversal, and unrestricted contraction remain outside scope.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The identification kernel is the exact support filter, sharp unrestricted-cone endpoints, and joint target-arm completion. For multivalued treatment, equivalence with Ban--Kédagni's all-arm class is claimed only when that class is nonempty; it is automatic on the binary submodel. The rational four-cell center and its open beta neighborhood, and the three-cell boundary family, are population results rather than empirical findings. The discontinuity and minimax theorem is SDC-only. Finite-sample projection covers the binary-treatment exact set, while a fully adaptive procedure and rate beyond the certified \(o(n^{-1/2})\) nonshrinking frontier remain open.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem identifies the exact statistical cost of a disappearing support-eligible branch through a root-\(n\) indistinguishable SDC experiment.
statement_notes.gap: Generic LP nonregularity does not provide this legal SDC family, its exact branch slacks and set jump, or the exact \(3/20\) known-pair minimax limit.
statement_notes.consumer: Inference procedures can be screened against a certified nonshrinking frontier even when the smallest positive branch slack is \(o(n^{-1/2})\).

statement_notes.justification: The coupling establishes joint target-arm attainment and also shows when the target-arm calculation is faithful to Ban--Kédagni's all-arm published class.
statement_notes.gap: Park2025 treats joint attainment under MIV plus MTR; it does not supply this conditional-product witness for armwise SDC, exact aggregate support, or extension from target-arm to all-arm restrictions.
statement_notes.consumer: Finite-valued-treatment users may report the exact ATE closure for the published all-arm class when that class is nonempty, while binary-treatment applications obtain the result without a class distinction.

proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(x=\mathbb E_Q[Y_1\mid(D,Z)=(0,0)]\) and \(y=\mathbb E_Q[Y_1\mid(D,Z)=(0,1)]\).  The cell probabilities in \(\text{def:strict-example}\) give
\[
 \mu_D=\frac{9}{25}+\frac{11}{100}=\frac{47}{100},
 \qquad
 \mu_Z=\frac{9}{20}+\frac{11}{100}=\frac{14}{25}.
\]
The two factual treated-cell means are \(79/100\) and \(17/20\).  Indeed, from the beta density definition, the mean is
\(B(\alpha+1,\beta)/B(\alpha,\beta)=\alpha/(\alpha+\beta)\).  Therefore the factual contribution to the arm-one mean is
\[
 c_1=\frac{9}{25}\frac{79}{100}+\frac{11}{100}\frac{17}{20}
     =\frac{3779}{10000},
\]
and consistency and the finite-cell decomposition in \(\text{lem:branch-reduction}\) give
\[
 \theta_1=\frac{3779}{10000}+\frac{2}{25}x+\frac{9}{20}y. \tag{1}
\]
Define the two SDC score moments
\[
 C_D=\operatorname{Cov}_Q(Y_1,D),
 \qquad C_Z=\operatorname{Cov}_Q(Y_1,Z).
\]
Since \(\mathbb E_Q[Y_1D]=c_1\) and
\(\mathbb E_Q[Y_1Z]=(9/20)y+(11/100)(17/20)\), direct substitution into the covariance definitions yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 C_D
   &=\frac{200287}{1000000}-\frac{47}{1250}x-\frac{423}{2000}y,\\
 C_Z
   &=-\frac{29531}{250000}-\frac{28}{625}x+\frac{99}{500}y.
 \end{aligned} \tag{2}
\]
Thus the positive branch is characterized by \(C_D\geq0,C_Z\geq0\), and the negative branch by \(C_D\leq0,C_Z\leq0\), exactly as in \(\text{def:branch-polytope}\).

Substitution into (1)--(2), with no rounding, gives
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
(x,y)&\theta_1&C_D&C_Z\\ \hline
\left(0,\frac{29531}{49500}\right)&\frac{711}{1100}&\frac{1019}{13750}&0\\[2pt]
\left(0,\frac{200287}{211500}\right)&\frac{3779}{4700}&0&\frac{2038}{29375}\\[2pt]
\left(1,\frac{54229}{70500}\right)&\frac{3779}{4700}&0&-\frac{312}{29375}\\[2pt]
\left(1,\frac{40731}{49500}\right)&\frac{911}{1100}&-\frac{78}{6875}&0
\end{array}. \tag{3}
\]
Consequently the first two vectors are feasible for the positive branch and the last two are feasible for the negative branch.

It remains to certify that the four feasible values in (3) are endpoints.  The two missing-cell SDC scores have common treatment coordinate \(-47/100\) and instrument coordinates \(-14/25\) and \(11/25\).  For
\[
 \lambda_Z=\left(0,\frac{25}{11}\right)'
\]
the two lower-dual box coefficients for the positive branch are
\[
 1-\lambda_Z's_{(0,0)}^{\mathrm{SDC}}=\frac{25}{11}>0,
 \qquad
 1-\lambda_Z's_{(0,1)}^{\mathrm{SDC}}=0. \tag{4}
\]
Hence the box minimization chooses \(x=0\) and is indifferent to \(y\).  At the first row of (3), the instrument score moment is zero, so the primal objective and the lower-dual objective at \(\lambda_Z\) coincide.  The equality \(L=V_L\) from \(\text{thm:cone-endpoint-sharpness}\) therefore proves that the first row attains \(L_{1,+}^{\mathrm{SDC}}(P^\star)=711/1100\).  For the negative branch, the upper-dual box coefficients are again those in (4); box maximization chooses \(x=1\), and the fourth row has zero instrument score moment.  The equality \(U=V_U\) therefore proves that the fourth row attains \(U_{1,-}^{\mathrm{SDC}}(P^\star)=911/1100\).

For the remaining two endpoints take
\[
 \lambda_D=\left(\frac{100}{47},0\right)'.
\]
Because both missing cells have treatment score \(-47/100\), the relevant upper-dual coefficients for the positive branch and lower-dual coefficients for the negative branch are, respectively,
\[
 1+\lambda_D's_j^{\mathrm{SDC}}=0,
 \qquad
 1+\lambda_D's_j^{\mathrm{SDC}}=0. \tag{5}
\]
The second and third rows of (3) have zero treatment score moment.  Primal and dual objectives hence coincide in (5), and \(\text{thm:cone-endpoint-sharpness}\) gives
\[
 U_{1,+}^{\mathrm{SDC}}(P^\star)
 =L_{1,-}^{\mathrm{SDC}}(P^\star)
 =\frac{3779}{4700}.
\]

Every displayed second coordinate lies strictly between zero and one.  Indeed, their respective distances to the nearer support endpoint are
\[
 \frac{19969}{49500},\qquad
 \frac{11213}{211500},\qquad
 \frac{16271}{70500},\qquad
 \frac{2923}{16500},
\]
all of which are positive.  Taking the corresponding slack coordinate equal to any of these positive distances verifies positive total interior slack under \(\text{def:interior-slack}\).  Finally,
\[
 \|\lambda_Z\|_1=\frac{25}{11}>1,
\]
so the two unrestricted-cone certificates for the outer sharp endpoints lie strictly outside the published normalized multiplier simplex.  This proves all assertions.

added_lemmas.statement:
In the family \(P^{\rho,s}\), the strictness witness is locally open rather than isolated.  At \((\rho,s)=(79/100,17/20)\), the positive and negative branch slacks satisfy
\[
 \tau_{1,+}^{\mathrm{SDC}}\geq\frac{19969}{49500},
 \qquad
 \tau_{1,-}^{\mathrm{SDC}}\geq\frac{2923}{16500}.
\]
The points \((x,y)=(1/2,3/4)\) and \((19/20,4/5)\) satisfy both score inequalities strictly in the positive and negative directions, respectively.  The endpoint multipliers \((0,25/11)'\) and \((100/47,0)'\) violate the normalized-simplex constraint by the positive \(\ell_1\)-margins \(14/11\) and \(53/47\).  The lower and upper gaps relative to the normalized outer union are, respectively,
\[
 \frac{711}{1100}-0.496024=\frac{206717}{1375000}>0,
 \qquad
 0.872824-\frac{911}{1100}=\frac{61383}{1375000}>0.
\]
Moreover, one may take \(\delta=1/100\): whenever \((\rho,s)\in(0,1)^2\) and
\(\max\{|\rho-79/100|,|s-17/20|\}<1/100\), both SDC branches are aggregate-support eligible and
\[
 \mathcal I_1^{\mathrm{SDC}}(P^{\rho,s})
 =\left[\frac{9\rho}{11},\frac{9\rho}{11}+\frac{2}{11}\right]
 \subsetneq \mathcal I_{BK}^{\rho,s}.
\]
At the center this recovers the exact rational closure \([711/1100,911/1100]\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Write
\[
 q(\rho,s)=\frac{9}{25}\rho+\frac{11}{100}s.
\]
At \((\rho,s)=(79/100,17/20)\), the two treated-cell laws in \(\text{def:parametric-strict-family}\) are \(\operatorname{Beta}(79,21)\) and \(\operatorname{Beta}(17,3)\).  The remaining conditional laws and all cell masses are fixed to those in \(\text{def:strict-example}\).  Hence
\[
 P^{79/100,17/20}=P^\star.
\]
The four cell masses, \(\mu_D=47/100\), \(\mu_Z=14/25\), and both missing-cell score vectors are constant throughout the family.  For missing means \((x,y)\in[0,1]^2\), the finite-cell moment decomposition gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \theta_1(\rho,s;x,y)
   &=q(\rho,s)+\frac{2}{25}x+\frac{9}{20}y,\\
 C_D(\rho,s;x,y)
   &=\frac{53}{100}q(\rho,s)
     -\frac{47}{100}\left(\frac{2}{25}x+\frac{9}{20}y\right),\\
 C_Z(\rho,s;x,y)
   &=\frac{11}{100}s-\frac{14}{25}q(\rho,s)
     -\frac{28}{625}x+\frac{99}{500}y.
 \end{aligned} \tag{6}
\]
These identities follow by expanding \(\mathbb E[Y_1D]-\mu_D\mathbb E[Y_1]\) and \(\mathbb E[Y_1Z]-\mu_Z\mathbb E[Y_1]\), respectively.

First record quantitative margins at the center.  The first and fourth endpoint certificates in \(\text{prop:rational-certificates}\) permit the feasible slack choices
\[
 (t_x,t_y)=\left(0,\frac{19969}{49500}\right)
 \quad\hbox{and}\quad
 (t_x,t_y)=\left(0,\frac{2923}{16500}\right),
\]
so the asserted lower bounds on \(\tau_{1,+}^{\mathrm{SDC}}\) and \(\tau_{1,-}^{\mathrm{SDC}}\) follow directly from \(\text{def:interior-slack}\).  Substitution into (6) gives
\[
 \begin{array}{c|cc}
 (x,y)&C_D&C_Z\\ \hline
 (1/2,3/4)&11431/500000&997/125000\\
 (19/20,4/5)&-4633/1000000&-571/250000
 \end{array}, \tag{7}
\]
which proves strict score feasibility with positive margins.  The multiplier margins are the exact calculations
\[
 \left\|\left(0,\frac{25}{11}\right)\right\|_1-1=\frac{14}{11},
 \qquad
 \left\|\left(\frac{100}{47},0\right)\right\|_1-1=\frac{53}{47}.
\]
Finally, \(\text{def:published-outer}\) and the center equality \(P^{79/100,17/20}=P^\star\), together with the exact endpoints from \(\text{prop:rational-certificates}\), give the two displayed positive outer-endpoint gaps.

We next exhibit the active bases that persist.  Define
\[
 z(\rho,s)=\frac{56}{55}\rho-\frac{11}{45}s,
 \qquad
 d(\rho,s)=\frac{53}{2115}(36\rho+11s). \tag{8}
\]
The four candidate endpoint vectors are
\[
 \begin{array}{c|cc}
 &x&y\\ \hline
 L_+&0&z(\rho,s)\\
 U_+&0&d(\rho,s)\\
 L_-&1&d(\rho,s)-8/45\\
 U_-&1&z(\rho,s)+112/495.
 \end{array} \tag{9}
\]
At the center, (9) is exactly the four-vector list in \(\text{prop:rational-certificates}\).  Equation (6) shows that the rows labeled \(L_+\) and \(U_-\) have \(C_Z=0\), whereas the rows labeled \(U_+\) and \(L_-\) have \(C_D=0\).  At the center, the nonbinding score coordinates, in row order, are
\[
 \frac{1019}{13750},\quad
 \frac{2038}{29375},\quad
 -\frac{312}{29375},\quad
 -\frac{78}{6875}. \tag{10}
\]
They have the strict signs required by their branches.  The four \(y\)-coordinates at the center have minimum distance
\[
 \min\left\{\frac{19969}{49500},\frac{11213}{211500},
              \frac{16271}{70500},\frac{2923}{16500}\right\}
 =\frac{11213}{211500}>0 \tag{11}
\]
from the relevant nearest box boundary.  Let \(\varepsilon=\max\{|\rho-79/100|,|s-17/20|\}\).  The center value of \(-27\rho+121s\) is \(2038/25\), its distance from \(94\) is \(312/25\), and its perturbation is at most \(148\varepsilon\).  Hence both signs in (10) persist when \(\varepsilon<1/100\).  The perturbations of \(z(\rho,s)\) and \(d(\rho,s)\) are at most \((125/99)\varepsilon\) and \((53/45)\varepsilon\), respectively.  At \(\varepsilon<1/100\), both bounds are smaller than the box margin in (11).  Thus all four rows in (9) remain feasible throughout the asserted neighborhood, and each branch remains aggregate-support eligible by \(\text{thm:support-eligibility}\).

The fixed multipliers \(\lambda_Z=(0,25/11)'\) and \(\lambda_D=(100/47,0)'\) used in the proof of \(\text{prop:rational-certificates}\) have coefficients depending only on the fixed missing-cell scores.  They therefore give the same primal--dual equalities for the four rows of (9).  By \(\text{thm:cone-endpoint-sharpness}\), these rows remain the four branch endpoints.  Substituting (8)--(9) into the first line of (6) yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 L_{1,+}^{\mathrm{SDC}}(P^{\rho,s})&=\frac{9\rho}{11},\\
 U_{1,+}^{\mathrm{SDC}}(P^{\rho,s})&=\frac{36\rho+11s}{47},\\
 L_{1,-}^{\mathrm{SDC}}(P^{\rho,s})&=\frac{36\rho+11s}{47},\\
 U_{1,-}^{\mathrm{SDC}}(P^{\rho,s})&=\frac{9\rho}{11}+\frac{2}{11}.
 \end{aligned} \tag{12}
\]
The two branch intervals meet at the middle value in (12).  The aggregate-support closure formula in \(\text{thm:support-eligibility}\) consequently proves
\[
 \mathcal I_1^{\mathrm{SDC}}(P^{\rho,s})
 =\left[\frac{9\rho}{11},\frac{9\rho}{11}+\frac{2}{11}\right] \tag{13}
\]
throughout the asserted max-norm neighborhood.  That neighborhood lies inside \((0,1)^2\); there all four Beta shape parameters are positive, and their densities are positive on \((0,1)\), so the observed conditional laws have support \([0,1]\), as required by the factual-support restriction.

It remains to prove that strict containment in the normalized outer union is stable.  For fixed \(b\), denote the lower and upper objective functions in \(\text{def:parametric-normalized-outer}\) by \(G_{L,b}(\lambda;\rho,s)\) and \(G_{U,b}(\lambda;\rho,s)\).  The box terms in these functions are independent of \((\rho,s)\), while \(c_1\) and \(h_1^{\mathrm{SDC}}\) are affine in \((\rho,s)\).  Hence, for either objective and center \((\rho_0,s_0)=(79/100,17/20)\),
\[
 \sup_{\lambda\in\Lambda_1}
 \left|G_{\cdot,b}(\lambda;\rho,s)-G_{\cdot,b}(\lambda;\rho_0,s_0)\right|
 \leq |c_1(\rho,s)-c_1(\rho_0,s_0)|
      +\|h_1^{\mathrm{SDC}}(\rho,s)-h_1^{\mathrm{SDC}}(\rho_0,s_0)\|_\infty,
 \tag{14}
\]
because \(\|\lambda\|_1\leq1\) on \(\Lambda_1\).  The right-hand side tends to zero.  The elementary inequalities
\[
 \left|\sup f-\sup g\right|\leq\sup|f-g|,
 \qquad
 \left|\inf f-\inf g\right|\leq\sup|f-g| \tag{15}
\]
therefore prove continuity of every normalized branch endpoint.  This is the required compact-parameter, or Berge-type, continuity conclusion, derived here directly from the finite dual formulas.  Finite minima and maxima of these four endpoints are continuous as well.

Restricting the dual multiplier domain from \(\mathbb R_+^2\) to \(\Lambda_1\) can only decrease a lower dual supremum and increase an upper dual infimum.  Therefore each normalized branch interval contains its exact branch interval in (12).  At the center, the equality just proved and the constructions in \(\text{def:parametric-normalized-outer}\) and \(\text{def:published-outer}\) show that the normalized union is \(\mathcal I_{BK}^\star\).  Thus the distance from the exact lower endpoint to the lower edge of the normalized union is \(206717/1375000\), and the distance from the exact upper endpoint to the upper edge is \(61383/1375000\).  More quantitatively, (6) implies
\[
 |c_1(\rho,s)-c_1(\rho_0,s_0)|\leq\frac{47}{100}\varepsilon,
 \qquad
 \|h_1^{\mathrm{SDC}}(\rho,s)-h_1^{\mathrm{SDC}}(\rho_0,s_0)\|_\infty
 \leq\frac14\varepsilon.
\]
Thus every normalized branch endpoint, and hence the minimum lower and maximum upper normalized endpoints, moves by at most \((18/25)\varepsilon\).  Either outer exact endpoint in (13) moves by at most \((9/11)\varepsilon\).  Each strict gap can consequently decrease by at most
\[
 \left(\frac{18}{25}+\frac{9}{11}\right)\varepsilon
 =\frac{423}{275}\varepsilon.
\]
For \(\varepsilon<1/100\), the smaller center gap remains at least
\[
 \frac{61383}{1375000}-\frac{423}{27500}
 =\frac{40233}{1375000}>0.
\]
Therefore (13) is contained branchwise in \(\mathcal I_{BK}^{\rho,s}\), while the normalized union still contains a point strictly below the left endpoint of (13) and a point strictly above its right endpoint.  This proves the strict inclusion on the stated neighborhood.  Substitution of \(\rho=79/100\) in (13) gives \([711/1100,911/1100]\), completing the proof.
